title: Non-contact Injury
note: Generated by tools/positions.py --extract from the page itself. Edit the verification, kind, signed_off_by and note fields; everything else is rewritten on the next extraction. positions.as_written: Ask whether anything or anybody hit the knee.
Ask what the foot was doing: planted, turning, or landing.
Ask what the body was doing: decelerating, changing direction, or landing from a jump.
Ask whether they heard or felt a pop, whether they fell, and whether they could carry on.
Ask about swelling timing, which is the single most discriminating follow-up.
A non-contact injury with valgus collapse should prompt a deliberate search for medial and rotational injury rather than a cruciate-only assessment.
- Valgus collapse should prompt a deliberate search for medial and rotational injury.
